headline: Geological Agency Confirms No Tsunami Risk After Banda Sea Quake
seoTitle: No Tsunami Risk Following 7.1 Magnitude Banda Sea Earthquake
metaDescription: Following a 7.1 magnitude earthquake in the Banda Sea, Indonesian authorities have confirmed there is no risk of a tsunami for the region.
aiSummaryBullets: A 7.1 magnitude earthquake struck the Banda Sea in Maluku on Tuesday morning.
Indonesian meteorological and geological agencies confirmed the event poses no tsunami risk.
Officials cited the 115-kilometer depth and strike-slip fault mechanism as reasons for the lack of tsunami potential.
aiContextParagraph: On November 17, 2026, a significant 7.1 magnitude earthquake occurred in the Banda Sea, impacting parts of Maluku Tenggara. The tremor was reportedly felt as far as Manokwari and various areas across Papua and Maluku. Following the initial seismic activity, residents in the affected region experienced panic, though local authorities have since reported that the situation has returned to a stable and conducive state. Both the Indonesian Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) and the Geological Agency provided technical assessments regarding the threat level. They concluded that there is no risk of a tsunami due to the earthquake's significant depth of approximately 115 kilometers beneath the surface and its specific strike-slip fault mechanism. Authorities continue to monitor the region for any subsequent activity following the seismic event.
whyItIsViral: This story is trending due to rapid coverage across five independent news outlets, indicating significant regional interest in the seismic event.
